results.title: How to Conduct and Analyze Semi-Structured Interviews - tools4dev
results.content: A semi-structured interview is one of the most effective tools for systematically gathering qualitative and quantitative data. This is a method which allows you to ask predetermined questions, determined, perhaps, by the theoretical framework or theory of change underpinning the project, or by your research hypothesis. There are a range of different analytic methods which could be applied to qualitative data, and choosing the right one will depend on the research you are conducting. If you have had a range of interviewers, you may want to spend some time just reading through all the data to try and gain a consistent view of the picture being painted by the data before beginning with the analysis. If you have a good idea of the overall implementation and research questions you hope to answer as you design the interview, it will then be much easier to understand what to do with your data.

results.title: Semi-Structured Interview | Definition, Guide & Examples
results.content: A **semi-structured interview** is a data collection method that relies on asking questions within a predetermined thematic framework. However, the questions are not set in order or in phrasing. In research, semi-structured interviews are often qualitative in nature. They are also common in field research with many interviewers, giving everyone the same theoretical framework, but allowing them to investigate different facets of the research question. Semi-structured interviews are a mix of structured and unstructured interviews. 1. What is a semi-structured interview? 5. Semi-structured interview questions. * Unlike in a structured interview, the phrasing and order of the questions is not set. However, since the questions are less set than in a structured interview, the data collection and analysis become a bit more complex. Semi-structured interviews are often considered “the best of both worlds.” Combining elements of structured and unstructured interviews gives semi-structured interviews the advantages of both: comparable, reliable data, and the flexibility to ask follow-up questions.
